title: Ostia (Confessions 9)
hookLine: Augustine and Monica, at a window, talk of heaven; days later she dies

lines: A MOTHER AND A SON, TALKING.
cards: Two people are leaning at a window that looks out on a garden. The house is in Ostia, the port of Rome. They're resting after a long journey overland, waiting for a ship to carry them home to Africa.
One is Augustine, newly baptized. The other is his mother, Monica, who wept and prayed over him through all his wandering. Nobody else is in the room.
And they begin to talk, quietly, about what the life of the saints with God might be like.

teach.h: THEIR TALK CLIMBS, STEP BY STEP.
teach.b: Augustine tells it in the ninth book of his Confessions.

Their talk climbs, step by step: past every pleasure of the body, past the beauty of earth and sky, sun and moon and stars, past even their own minds, reaching toward the Wisdom by which all things are made.

And for a moment, he writes, they touched it, just barely, with the whole force of the heart. Then they sighed, and came back down to the sound of their own voices, to words that have a beginning and an end.
He wonders what it would be like if that moment simply went on, and reaches for Jesus's words in Matthew's Gospel, in the King James: "enter thou into the joy of thy lord." Then Monica speaks.
Son, she says, nothing in this life delights me anymore. What am I still doing here? There was one thing I wanted to stay for: to see you a Christian before I died.
God has given me that, and more. Days later, she falls ill with a fever. Near the end, one of her sons wishes she could die in her own country, not in a strange place.
She waves it away. Lay this body anywhere, she says.
Only remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you are. Augustine holds back his tears at her burial, and later, alone, lets them come. Notice where this reaching for God happens.
Not in a desert, not in a church. At a window, in a borrowed house, between a mother and a son who had been far apart and found their way back, just talking about what mattered.

how: Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican Christians remember Monica as a saint, often as a patron of mothers who pray for their children; the scene at Ostia is read as part of Augustine's Confessions.

o: the North African town where Augustine was born
the church in Milan where Monica was buried
the port of Rome where Augustine and Monica talked

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: nothing in this life delights me

s: at Ostia, Augustine was alone with God
he was with his mother, Monica, talking at a window.
Monica asked to be buried in her homeland
she said to lay her body anywhere, and remember her at the altar of the Lord.
Augustine says they touched it only for a moment
then they sighed and came back down to words with a beginning and an end.

games.q: you're Monica, ill, far from home. one of your sons wishes you could die at home, not in a strange place. what do you say?
o: take me home and bury me in Africa.
lay this body anywhere; remember me at the altar.
don't think about me at all.
games.why: she let go of the grave and asked only to be remembered at the altar of the Lord, wherever they were.

practice: Picture someone you love beside you at a window, with nowhere to be: a parent, a child, a friend, a partner.
Find one question you'd want to ask them, about what they hope for, what they're grateful for, or what they think happens at the end, and hear yourself asking it gently.
If you pray, hold them before God; if you don't, hold them in your attention.

wordCard.voice: Ostia. The port where Augustine and Monica, at a window, reached for God together, days before she died.

orig.note: Greek: joy. the word in enter thou into the joy of thy lord, the line Augustine reaches for at the window.

carryVoice: Your line: at the window. A borrowed house, a quiet talk, and a moment of reaching for God. Day seven hundred eighty.
